precepts.text: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. That was the attribute Job had, and we have to be the same way.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

That was the attribute Job had: “the cause which I knew not I searched out.” The Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind, and they searched the scriptures daily to see whether the things they were taught were so. That made them more noble.

We have to be the same way. Search things out daily. Do not just hear it and move on, and do not come asking without having looked first. A father to the poor, a judge in the gate, and a man who searched out what he did not know: that is the kind of man Job was, and the kind we have to become.

precepts.text: The Bereans were more noble because they received the word with all readiness of mind and searched the scriptures daily; search daily and you will be vexed with the world, or else the world's words fill your ears.
precepts.point: Sin becomes repulsive only when the word of God is in you; without reading and studying, the sins of the world become normal to you as to everybody else.
precepts.why:
God “delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked”. Examine yourself: are you vexed with the filthy conversation of this world? Or are you up late scrolling, looking at booties, two hours in the middle of the night on your phone? Those two hours you could have read the Bible. If you can't sleep, pick up the Bible; half of one chapter and the demon will put you to sleep. In time the Most High will wake up your spirit, and you will read one, two, three, four chapters.

“For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day”. Every day you wake up you should be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. But to be vexed, you have to be in this Bible. It is by having the word of God in you that sin starts becoming repulsive. If you are not reading and not studying, the sins of the world will be normal to you, just like everybody else. The Lord saved a remnant, and that is why we did not become as Sodom and Gomorrha. What is that remnant doing? Studying day and night.

Paul and Silas were sent by night unto Berea and went into the synagogue, and “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” If you are searching the scriptures daily, you will be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. If you are not, whose words are going to be in your ears? The TV, the street, your phone: the ways of this world.

God turned Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes, “making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. America read the example and legalized gay marriage anyway, a habitual line stepper pushing the envelope until his sin reached the heavens. Only the one searching the scriptures daily will be vexed like Lot and delivered like Lot.

precepts.why:
“Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.” We are literally the offspring of God, and idols are not him. “And the times of this ignorance God winked at”: he had mercy and was longsuffering with us, “but now commandeth all men every where to repent”, all Israelite men everywhere.

How do we answer that command? “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. The Bible tells the Israelites to gather together, not to be separate individuals. That is for all of you online who like to stay home and say, I don't like camps. Do what God said to do. Come in, learn, sit down and be quiet.

Some say, I want to come to the school, but I'm not right yet; I'll come when I get right. When is that going to be? You come to the school to get right; none of us are 100% right, we're all trying to get right. You aren't going to get right in your wicked mama's house or with your homeboys. Not gathering shows you love Babylon and white Jesus, that you're okay with black people shot down in the streets and on drugs, and it delays the coming of Christ.

Gather “Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. Then: “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment”, the curses of Deuteronomy 28; “seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” Joel says the same: “Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children”, and let the priests cry, “Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them”.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
The Lord said, “Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun”, and Moses said to the judges, “Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor”: every judge by his rank, the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant.

The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ. “Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device. And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent.” The times of this ignorance He winked at: the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism.

But now He commandeth all men every where to repent, “Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.” That man is Jesus the Christ.

Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

precepts.why:
Sopater of Berea was the first name, so here is Berea. “And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.” Paul went into a synagogue of the Jews. “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica,” The Jews that were in Berea were more noble than the Jews in Thessalonica. How so? “in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” They received what Paul was teaching with all readiness of mind, but they continued searching the scriptures daily whether such things were so.

“Therefore many of them believed;” Many of them, and guess who one of them was: Sopater, the name we just read from Berea, was one of them which believed. “also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
Now Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica. “Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,” Three sabbath days Paul reasoned with them out of the scriptures. “Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ. And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.”

So out of Thessalonica, notice these people that believed: two of the names we just read, Aristarchus and Secundus, helped Paul set up the seven churches of Asia Minor. What always catches the eye is that you had chief women in the church; that is Titus 2, those are the chief women. And it talks about the Greeks, which we deal with a little later on.
